promise: AI hacks, future drops & tech tea
Clean, funny, made in Nairobi for the world
posts.community: Follow & join the Wanakesho: the ones building tomorrow.
posts.caption:
Sasa, Wanakesho! AI hacks, future drops and tech tea, in Kenyan English, zero boring lectures. Drop the one tech thing you wish someone explained properly and we'll cover it this week.

#JuaKesho #Wanakesho

posts.title: Turn a 1-hour lecture into notes in 2 minutes
moves: Record the lecture on your phone (ask the lecturer first).
Upload the audio to an AI that takes voice files, like Gemini.
Ask: “Bullet notes + 5 exam questions, simple English.”
posts.caption:
AI Hack: a 1-hour lecture into clean notes and practice questions in about 2 minutes. Always ask before recording. Send this to the class group before CATs.

#AIHack #JuaKesho

posts.meaning: What you type to tell an AI what you want. Vague prompt, vague answer. Give it a role, a task and an example.
posts.try_this: Not “write a caption” but “3 funny captions for my thrift reel, Kenyan English, under 12 words”.
posts.caption:
Decode No. 1: Prompt. The difference between a boring AI answer and a fire one is how you ask. Save this, then share your best prompt in the comments.

#Decode #JuaKesho

posts.claim: You need to know coding to build with AI.
posts.real: Most AI tools work in plain English. Coding takes you further, but you can build a bot, a site or a content system this weekend without it.
posts.source: General: mainstream AI assistants and no-code automation tools accept plain-language instructions
posts.caption:
Cap or No Cap? “You need coding to build with AI.” CAP. Start with plain English, learn code as you go. Tag the friend who keeps saying “I'm not a tech person”.

#CapOrNoCap #JuaKesho

posts.title: “Get paid to like TikToks”
posts.sms: Hi! Earn Ksh 2,000 daily liking videos. Pay Ksh 500 registration to start today.
tips: Real jobs never ask you to pay to start.
Nobody pays you just to like posts.
posts.source: Common 'task scam' pattern (pay-to-start online jobs); confirm against a current Communications Authority of Kenya or Safaricom fraud advisory before posting
posts.caption:
USIIBIWE! “Earn daily for liking videos, just pay registration.” That's how they get you. Real jobs don't charge you to start. Send this to the group chat, someone needs it.

#Usiibiwe #JuaKesho

posts.title: 40 applications, 0 replies

right.say: Same CV for every job? Let AI tailor it to each one.

posts.caption:
Vichekesho: same CV for 40 jobs = 0 replies. Tailor it per job with AI, keep every fact true. Tag the friend currently on application number 41.

#Vichekesho #JuaKesho

posts.pov: your AI agent applied to 20 jobs while you slept, each cover letter in your voice.
posts.real: Early AI agents that do tasks for you already exist. The skill that pays: telling them exactly what you want, then checking their work.
posts.source: General: AI assistants that can take multi-step actions ('agents') are available in early form from major AI companies
posts.caption:
POV: Kesho. Your AI agent job-hunting while you sleep. Closer than you think. Would you trust it? Reply YES or NO.

#POVKesho #JuaKesho

posts.hook: I got tired of PDF timetables…
posts.title: So I built a bot that reads campus notices for me
posts.result: Pilot soon. Comment BOT for the breakdown.
posts.caption:
Build With Me: a bot that reads campus notices so nobody digs through PDFs again. No human, no send: every message gets approved first. Comment BOT and we'll break it down step by step.

#BuildWithMe #JuaKesho

posts.name: M-Pesa
posts.fact: Kenya made sending money by SMS an everyday thing, long before most of the world had heard of mobile money.
posts.now: We started it. The world followed.
posts.caption:
Made in Africa: in 2007 Kenya launched M-Pesa, and sending money by phone became normal here. Which African innovation are you proud of? Drop it in the comments.

#MadeInAfrica #JuaKesho

Kesho Kutwa: 5 things your phone will soon do for you. Swipe, then save it so you remember when tomorrow comes.

#KeshoKutwa #JuaKesho

posts.headline: Your phone will be your translator.
posts.leo: Apps can already translate a live conversation between many languages, Kiswahili included.
posts.kesho: Talk to anyone, anywhere, each in your own language, almost without noticing the phone.
posts.anza: Open Google Translate, tap Conversation, and chat with a friend in two languages.
posts.caption:
1/5: Your phone will be your translator. Try Conversation mode in Google Translate today, then send this to the friend who travels most.

#KeshoKutwa #JuaKesho

posts.thing: wait for radio to “discover” new artists
posts.old: Burn the song, beg a DJ, wait months, hope.
posts.new: Upload to streaming, turn the hook into a TikTok sound, pitch playlists from your artist dashboard, study your fan data.
posts.cta: Tag an artist who needs this.
posts.source: General: major streaming platforms offer artist dashboards with playlist pitching and listener data
posts.caption:
Still in 2026? Waiting for radio to find you. The kesho way: your fans are already on TikTok and streaming. Tag an upcoming artist who needs this, then drop your favourite new Kenyan song below.

#StillIn2026 #JuaKesho

posts.name: Ushahidi
posts.what: Open-source software built in Kenya that lets people report what's happening by SMS or web, and see it on a live map.
posts.why: Made here, then used by responders and communities around the world. Proof that African tech travels.
posts.cta: Share this so more people know it's ours.
posts.caption:
Put Us On: Ushahidi, built in Kenya in 2008, now used around the world. We support our own. Share this, then tag an African startup or artist we should spotlight next.

#PutUsOn #JuaKesho

posts.what: 59% of the Sh515bn set aside for 14 flagship projects over five years was never used, says the Auditor-General.
posts.why: Unused money still costs: loans on undrawn funds charge fees, and the projects you were promised wait.
posts.check: Auditor-General reports are public on parliament.go.ke. Read one page tonight.
posts.source: Auditor-General Nancy Gathungu to the National Assembly Budget Committee, 2 June 2025 (Capital FM: capitalfm.africa/audit-exposes-sh304bn-in-idle-govt-project-funds)
posts.caption:
Follow the Money: Sh304 billion set aside for flagship projects, never used. Unused money still costs us in loan fees and delayed projects. Save this and send it to someone who says “politics isn't my business”. It's your money.

#FollowTheMoney #JuaKesho

posts.title: How to spot a paid hashtag in 30 seconds
moves: Same phrase, many accounts, same hour? Copy-paste army.
Tap the profiles: new, few real followers, posts only hashtags.
Search the tag, sort by oldest: see who started it and when.
posts.payoff: Some get paid $10–15 a day to trend.
posts.source: Mozilla Foundation, 'Inside the Shadowy World of Disinformation-for-hire in Kenya', Odanga Madung & Brian Obilo, 2 Sept 2021
posts.caption:
See Through It: some trends are bought. Mozilla researchers documented influencers paid via M-Pesa to push hashtags. Before you retweet, check in 30 seconds. Send this to the group chat that believes every trend.

#SeeThroughIt #JuaKesho

posts.title: The Ksh 500 “job”

left.sms: Kazi ya leo: come make noise tomorrow. Ksh 500 + lunch. Don't ask questions.

right.say: 500 today. Who pays if things go wrong?

left.say: Blocked. My future costs more than 500.

posts.source: Allegory: fictional characters. Pattern of paying young people to disrupt or crowd events is widely reported in Kenyan media and civil society research
posts.caption:
Vichekesho: the Ksh 500 “job”. Nobody who pays you to shout cares what happens to you after. Fictional characters, real pattern. Send this to a friend who's worth more than 500.

#SeeThroughIt #JuaKesho

posts.kicker: Wake up. Build. Do it right.
posts.caption:
Africa can't wait. Not for permission, not for “next year”. Tomorrow is already here, and it belongs to the ones who learn it first. Send this to one person who's ready to build.

#JuaKesho #Wanakesho

posts.claim: Africa is basically one country with one culture.
posts.who: a stereotype still found in comments
posts.claim_source: Recurring stereotype in comment sections and old textbooks; not attributed to one person
proof: 54 countries, each with its own government, flag and story.
Over 2,000 languages: roughly a third of all the languages spoken on Earth.
Kenya alone speaks 40+ languages, and Sheng belongs to all of us.
posts.source: UN member states by region (un.org/en/about-us/member-states); Ethnologue, languages of Africa (ethnologue.com)
posts.caption: Set It Straight: Africa is not a country. It's 54 of them, and more languages than any other continent. Send this to the friend who still says 'I'm going to Africa' like it's one town.\n\n#SetItStraight #JuaKesho

posts.message: Cloud storage keeps your files safe off your phone, like a stage keeps passengers moving.
posts.like: a matatu stage for your files
posts.explain: Your photos and notes wait at a safe stage online. Lose the phone? Your files are still there. Log in from any phone and pick them up.
posts.caption:
Cloud storage, explained the Kenyan way. Turn on Google Photos or iCloud backup today, then send this to the friend who lost everything with their last phone.

#JuaKesho
